run: architecture candidate 5: the cluster and modulation engines on the dev cases, synthetic known answers and both fixtures; today's tool summaries against the new renderers on 1,010 tool results; arms A and A+ on the dev set, before and after, 2026-10-19
evidence: Candidate 5 (docs/AGENT_PLAN.md, sections B and C): the cluster and modulation decisions lived in the Copilot tool (copilotTools.js summarizeClusters / summarizeModulations), and arm A+ re-derived them with rules of its own (no trigonality; rigidity blocked by arm A's split-site rule and by breathing, but not by a pattern), so the control arm and the tool could disagree; analyze_clusters asked the engine twice, and when its second ('sites') request failed the split-site note was dropped silently and split sites could read as rigid (dev-jahn-teller's F octahedra are the case it protects). After the change the engines decide (Findings with recomputable Evidence, the tool's rules ported rule for rule): today's summaries and the new renderers give the same data and checks on 1,010 tool results (the Demo, the dev cases, both fixtures and 12 random configurations over a grid of windows); the model-visible snapshots pass without -u; Python and JS agree on every verdict of both fixtures, which refuse a decided statistic within 1e-6 of its threshold; the Python known answers (tests/test_clusters.py, test_modulations.py, test_clusters_api.py) and the JS ones below hold. Arms A and A+ on the dev set: every score and claim unchanged; only the nine A+ records' cluster and modulation readings change. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
proposed_fix: cluster_distortion (clusters.py, workers/clusters.js) always returns a verdict: distorted, lessDistorted, breathing, rigid, staticDistortion, splitMemberSites, trigonalLean, favouredAxes and the window, each {answer, because, evidence}, read from the unrounded statistics by CLUSTER_RULES (echoed); the split rule (isSplitSite) moves into the cluster engine and list_sites imports it. displacement_modulations gives each tested point sigma (+inf as SIGMA_MAX = 40, -inf as null, as the tool showed them), kind, ordered, because and bar, each element {cellDoubling, generalOrder, longWave} with decidedBy and the nearest miss, and the payload family and rules; one long-wave predicate. The tools render the verdicts through sentence tables keyed by (finding, because); arm A+ maps the answers to claims (distorted, breathing, rigid; a cell doubling or general order as a modulation at its q). No model-visible change. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19; the user may reverse it.
